newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on doller sales.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on doller sales.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee closed up as banks sold dollars to generate rupees as call money rates continued to rise, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 58.32 to the dollar, after opening at 58.46, they said.
"The dollar fell as high call rates led to banks unwinding dollar positions," said a Commercial Bank dealer. "There was no significant commercial demand to support the dollar either," he said.
Overnight call money rates closed at 17 percent after opening at 15, dealers said.

"Call rates are high as money is tight due to the cumulative impact of quarterly tax payments, excessive holidays when there are high cash withdrawals and banks covering imports with dollars from the Central Bank, all happening in the last three weeks," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
